topics.name: Moonshine Speech-to-Text
topics.summary: On-device ASR leveraging encoder-only transformers and speculative decoding for sub-100ms latency.
topics.mechanics: Replaces the standard encoder-decoder architecture with an encoder-only transformer to eliminate cross-attention overhead. Implements speculative token verification where a small draft model proposes tokens that are verified in parallel by the main model, reducing sequential decoding steps. Uses dynamic sequence bucketing to optimize memory access patterns and batch processing for variable-length audio inputs on edge hardware.
topics.tradeoffs: Achieves 5x lower latency than Whisper, targeting sub-100ms real-time transcription. Trade-off involves potential accuracy degradation compared to larger decoder-based models due to the encoder-only constraint and reliance on speculative sampling correctness.
topics.comparison: Whisper uses a heavy encoder-decoder architecture with sequential autoregressive decoding, resulting in higher latency and memory footprint. Moonshine's encoder-only design and speculative verification significantly reduce compute per token, making it viable for real-time on-device use where Whisper is typically too slow or resource-intensive.

topics.name: AI Guardrails
topics.summary: Pre/post-processing filters using regex, LLM-as-judge, and vector similarity to enforce safety policies.
topics.mechanics: Implements a multi-layered pipeline: (1) Deterministic regex/keyword matching for PII and banned terms (microseconds); (2) Embedding-based semantic drift detection against a 'safe' vector space (milliseconds); (3) Small LLM (e.g., Llama-3-8B) classification for nuanced toxicity or hallucination checks. Operates as a sidecar or middleware intercepting request/response streams.
topics.tradeoffs: Adds 50-200ms latency per turn if using LLM-based checks. Trade-off: High recall on semantic violations vs. increased inference cost. Deterministic layers are near-zero cost but low recall for obfuscated attacks.
topics.comparison: Superior to simple keyword blocking by catching semantic evasion and context-aware toxicity. More expensive than no guardrails but significantly reduces legal/liability risk compared to raw model outputs.

topics.name: Synthetic Data
topics.summary: Programmatic generation of edge-case and distribution-shifted data to augment training and eval sets.
topics.mechanics: Uses LLMs to generate variations of seed data via prompt engineering (paraphrasing, adversarial perturbation, persona simulation). Includes a 'filter' stage using embedding distance or classifier scores to ensure generated samples are distinct from real data and within desired difficulty bounds. Often used for RLHF preference pair generation.
topics.tradeoffs: Cost: $0.01-$0.10 per 1k samples depending on model size. Trade-off: Risk of 'model collapse' if synthetic data dominates training set without real-data anchoring. High throughput allows rapid iteration on eval suites (10x faster than manual labeling).
topics.comparison: Faster and cheaper than human annotation for long-tail edge cases. Less reliable for factual accuracy than human-verified data, but superior for testing robustness and diversity of model behavior.

topics.name: AI Inference Optimization
topics.summary: Hardware-aware kernel fusion, quantization (INT8/FP8), and speculative decoding to maximize tokens/sec.
topics.mechanics: Leverages vLLM/TensorRT-LLM for PagedAttention (reducing KV cache memory fragmentation by 2-4x). Applies FP8/INT8 quantization to weights and activations. Implements speculative decoding: a small draft model generates k tokens, verified in parallel by the large target model, reducing latency by 2-3x for coherent text. Continuous batching maximizes GPU utilization by packing requests dynamically.
topics.tradeoffs: FP8 quantization reduces memory footprint by ~50% with <1% accuracy loss. Speculative decoding adds complexity but cuts p95 latency by 40-60%. Trade-off: Quantization may degrade performance on math/code tasks; speculative decoding requires careful draft model selection to avoid high rejection rates.
topics.comparison: Significantly outperforms naive HuggingFace Transformers pipelines (5-10x throughput). More complex to deploy than single-model serving but essential for cost-effective high-concurrency production environments.

topics.name: Graph-Based Agent Orchestration
topics.summary: Stateful DAG execution where nodes are LLM calls/tools and edges define conditional control flow.
topics.mechanics: Models agent workflows as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) or state machine. Each node represents an atomic action (LLM call, API tool, human-in-the-loop). Edges are conditional transitions based on node output (e.g., 'if confidence < 0.8, route to human'). Supports parallel execution of independent branches and checkpointing for fault tolerance. Uses a central state store (Redis/Postgres) to persist intermediate results.
topics.tradeoffs: Adds 10-50ms overhead per node transition for state serialization/deserialization. Trade-off: Increased complexity vs. linear chains; enables complex multi-step reasoning with error recovery. Parallel branches can reduce wall-clock time but increase peak concurrent LLM calls (cost spike).
topics.comparison: More robust and debuggable than recursive ReAct loops, which can get stuck in infinite cycles. Enables deterministic fallback paths and parallelism, unlike simple sequential agent chains.

topics.name: AI Sovereignty and Semiconductor Competition
topics.summary: Geopolitical fragmentation of compute supply chains forcing architectural decoupling from US-centric silicon.
topics.mechanics: Shift from monolithic H100/H200 clusters to heterogeneous, regionally constrained hardware stacks. Requires abstraction layers (e.g., Triton, ONNX) to decouple model inference from specific CUDA kernels. Involves managing latency variance across different interconnects (NVLink vs. proprietary domestic interconnects) and implementing model quantization (INT8/INT4) to compensate for lower FLOPS density in non-leading edge nodes.
topics.tradeoffs: Trade-off: 15-30% reduction in peak throughput on non-NVIDIA domestic chips vs. 100% regulatory compliance. Latency spikes of 20-50ms when crossing data center boundaries due to sovereignty-enforced data residency. Memory bandwidth becomes the primary bottleneck, not compute, in sovereign stacks.
topics.comparison: Incumbent: Globalized, NVIDIA-centric cloud architecture. New: Regionalized, multi-vendor silicon strategy with higher operational complexity but lower geopolitical risk. Requires dual-stack deployment pipelines.

topics.name: Moving from AI Experimentation to Measurable Business Value
topics.summary: Transitioning from qualitative demo metrics to quantitative ROI tracking via automated evaluation pipelines.
topics.mechanics: Implementation of continuous evaluation loops using LLM-as-a-Judge and human-in-the-loop sampling. Requires instrumenting every inference call with metadata (token count, latency, user feedback) stored in a vector database or data lake. Shifts focus from 'model accuracy' to 'task completion rate' and 'cost per resolved ticket'. Involves building A/B testing frameworks for prompt variations and model versions.
topics.tradeoffs: Key Metric: Cost per successful task (e.g., $0.05 per resolved support ticket). Trade-off: High initial engineering cost for eval infrastructure vs. long-term reduction in hallucination-related support costs. Latency overhead of 5-10% for real-time evaluation logging.
topics.comparison: Incumbent: Siloed experimentation with no feedback loop to production. New: Closed-loop system where production data directly informs model fine-tuning and prompt optimization, creating a compounding value curve.

topics.name: Why Most AI Agents Fail in Production
topics.summary: Failure stems from unbounded state management, lack of error recovery, and hallucinated tool usage.
topics.mechanics: Agents fail due to 'context rot' where long conversation histories degrade reasoning quality. Lack of deterministic error handling when tool calls fail (e.g., API timeout). Over-reliance on single-shot reasoning without iterative self-correction. Memory management is often naive (sliding window) rather than hierarchical (short-term vs. long-term vector memory). No circuit breakers for infinite loops in agent decision trees.
topics.tradeoffs: Failure Rate: 40-60% of agent tasks fail in production without robust error handling. Latency: Multi-step agents can take 10-30 seconds per task, requiring asynchronous execution patterns. Trade-off: Complexity of state management vs. reliability. Need for explicit 'stop conditions' and 'fallback paths'.
topics.comparison: Incumbent: Simple RAG or single-turn LLM calls. New: Stateful, multi-step agents with persistent memory and error recovery. Requires significant investment in orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI) and monitoring.

topics.name: MCP vs Function Calling vs API Integration
topics.summary: MCP standardizes tool discovery and invocation, reducing custom integration overhead compared to raw function calling.
topics.mechanics: Function Calling: LLM outputs JSON schema, app parses and executes. MCP: Client-server protocol where tools are discovered dynamically via a standardized interface. MCP abstracts the tool definition, allowing any MCP-compliant client to use any MCP-compliant server. Reduces code duplication and enables modular tool ecosystems. Function calling is simpler but requires manual schema management for each tool.
topics.tradeoffs: MCP adds 5-10ms latency for tool discovery but reduces development time by 50% for multi-tool integrations. Trade-off: Standardization overhead vs. flexibility. Function calling is faster for single-tool use cases but scales poorly with 10+ tools.
topics.comparison: Incumbent: Custom API integrations with hardcoded schemas. New: MCP-based dynamic tool discovery. Enables plug-and-play tool ecosystems, reducing maintenance burden and improving scalability.
